sections.h2: How fast is St. Johns County growing?
sections.html:
St. Johns County is one of the faster-growing counties in Florida, up 26.7 percent between the April 2020 base of 273,426 and the July 2025 estimate of 346,328. For a seller, growth means a lot of recent construction nearby: the Census Bureau counted 4,735 building permits in 2025.

St. Johns spans about 600.6 square miles of land, with 455.2 residents per square mile in 2020. Owners live in 82.2 percent of the homes, so most competing listings are single-family homes. The table gives the main numbers.

sections.h2: Which office does what on a St. Johns County property tax bill?
sections.html:
The Saint Johns County Property Appraiser values the property and handles exemptions, while the county tax collector mails the bill in November. The appraiser's website also hosts a property tax estimator, a new-owner guide and a property damage guide, all useful when a house changes hands.

The Value Adjustment Board hears disputes about value or exemption denials, and the clerk of court records the deed. Taxing bodies, including the school board and municipalities, set the millage rates after public hearings advertised on the TRIM notice.

sections.h2: What are the key property tax dates in St. Johns County?
sections.html:
The appraiser's date page gives the cycle: January 1 sets the status and condition of the property, and March 1 is the filing deadline for homestead and other personal exemptions, agricultural classification and organizational exemptions. Tangible personal property returns for businesses are filed between January 1 and April 1.

Notices of proposed taxes arrive in August or September, and they list public hearing dates on millage. Tax bills follow in November. The 2026 deadline was moved to March 2 because March 1 fell on a weekend, which the office explains as the rule when the date lands on a weekend.

  • January 1: condition and ownership fix eligibility.
  • March 1 (or next business day): exemption filing.
  • April 1: business personal property returns.
  • August to September: TRIM notices.
  • November: bills mailed.

sections.h2: What is the St. Johns County homestead exemption worth?
sections.html:
For tax year 2026 the appraiser prints a total homestead exemption of $51,411. The first $25,000 reaches all taxes including school taxes, and the remaining $26,411 applies to assessed value between $50,000 and $75,000, excluding school taxes.

You must own the home and live there as your permanent residence on January 1. The office asks for a Florida driver license or ID showing the homestead address and Social Security numbers for the applicant and spouse. A trust owner who is not a trustee may need to supply the trust. Placing the home in an LLC ends the exemption and removes caps, because the office treats that as a change of ownership.

Late filers with just cause can apply until the end of the TRIM period, typically late August.

sections.h2: What happens to the Save Our Homes cap when a St. Johns County house sells?
sections.html:
The buyer starts over, and the seller may take the benefit along. A homesteaded property's assessed value cannot rise more than 3 percent or the CPI change, whichever is less, but a sale resets the property to market value on the next January 1.

The seller can move up to $500,000 of accumulated difference to a new Florida home through portability. St. Johns County's appraiser says the transfer must occur within three tax years, counted January through December from the sale, and a December sale counts as one tax year. If you downsize, the benefit is scaled by the ratio of the new just value to the old one. All owners of the old home who also own the new one must apply together. Portability does not cross state lines. Non-homestead property has a separate 10 percent cap that cannot be ported.

sections.h2: What do deed taxes and recording cost on a St. Johns County sale?
sections.html:
Seventy cents for each $100 of price is the stamp rate, and no surtax follows it here because the Miami-Dade schedule is the only exception. The department of revenue says every party named on the deed shares liability, so settle the question in writing.

Statute puts the clerk's first page at $5.00 and later pages at $4.00, with trust fund and technology additions. A mortgage that stays on the house counts toward the price. A spouse-to-spouse deed whose only consideration is the mortgage on the marital homestead is listed as exempt.

sections.h2: How can a St. Johns County owner dispute an assessment?
sections.html:
File a petition with the Value Adjustment Board within 25 days of the TRIM notice, using one of the DR-486 forms, which the state says go to the clerk. The notice itself prints the exact deadline, so check it the day it arrives.

The appraiser's site has a Value Adjustment Board page and a Property Owner Bill of Rights for owners who want to understand the process first. If the dispute is a denied exemption, classification or portability claim, the state allows a petition in the 30 days after a denial letter goes out. A seller who thinks the value is too high should raise it before listing, since a lower assessed value changes the buyer's carrying cost estimate.

sections.h2: Which other exemptions apply to St. Johns County sellers and buyers?
sections.html:
The appraiser lists other exemptions and an agricultural classification on separate pages, and the state adds age and veteran benefits. Some 22.5 percent of residents are 65 and over, so the senior options are worth a look.

  • Age 65 or older: local ordinances may allow an added homestead exemption of up to $50,000 when household income is within the limit.
  • Disabled former servicemembers with a rating of 10 percent or more: a $5,000 reduction in assessed value.
  • Veterans 65 or older with a permanent service-connected disability: a discount equal to the disability percentage on homestead.
  • Deployed servicemembers: an exemption matching the share of the prior year deployed.

A buyer who closes after January 1 cannot claim homestead for that year, so ask the appraiser how the first partial year will be billed.

sections.h2: What if taxes go unpaid on a St. Johns County property?
sections.html:
The unpaid balance becomes delinquent April 1, and certificates must be sold on unpaid items by June 1. A title company will want the balance cleared out of the seller's proceeds.

A certificate holder may apply for a tax deed once two years pass from April 1 of the issue year, paying a $75 application fee. Where the land is homestead, the starting bid adds half of the latest assessed value. Homestead owners can ask the tax collector about deferral by March 31.

  • Obtain a payoff statement early.
  • Ask whether any certificate exists on the parcel.
  • Check the escrow account when a lender pays.

faqs.q: What is the 2026 homestead exemption total in St. Johns County?
faqs.a: $51,411, as printed by the St. Johns County Property Appraiser: $25,000 on all taxes and $26,411 on non-school taxes over $50,000 of assessed value.

faqs.q: When is the exemption deadline in St. Johns County?
faqs.a: March 1, or the next business day when it falls on a weekend, which made it March 2 in 2026. Late filers with just cause can apply until the TRIM period ends.

faqs.q: Does a St. Johns County buyer inherit the seller's capped value?
faqs.a: No. The sale resets the property to market value the next January 1, and the seller's cap and exemptions end with the sale.

faqs.q: Can I rent out my St. Johns County homestead?
faqs.a: Renting the whole home for more than 30 days in two consecutive tax years can cost you the exemption, according to the appraiser. Renting a garage apartment removes only that part.

faqs.q: Is there a deed tax on St. Johns County sales?
faqs.a: Yes. Documentary stamp tax is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, paid to the clerk at the recording counter.
